A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Procgen-HD resolution-scaling study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PPO experiments across Procgen-HD environments, architectural comparisons, saliency and dormant-neuron analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds architectural ablations, per-layer dormant-neuron results, and higher-resolution Starpilot experiments.

M1.justification: The central PPO and Impoola procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B.1.2 adds architectural adaptations for controlled testing: stronger early downsampling, larger convolution kernels, 50-dimensional projections, and DrQ-v2-style LayerNorm/Tanh bottlenecks, including bottleneck variants of Impoola.

E1.justification: The same 16 environments and training tracks remain. Appendix B.1.4 extends actual evaluation to native resolutions of 128, 160, 192, 224, and 256 on hard Starpilot with Impoola. v1's 192-resolution images were illustrative rather than evaluated; no new application domain is tested.

E2.justification: Figure 15 substantially expands the architectural comparison set with downsampling, 5×5-kernel, reduced-projection, and DrQ-v2-style Impala variants, plus reduced-bottleneck Impoola variants. SoftMoE and four-ConvSeq networks already appeared in v1. The new DrQ-v2-style comparator adapts its bottleneck within PPO; it is not an evaluation of the complete DrQ-v2 algorithm.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled architectural comparisons at width 3 and resolutions 64/96. It also revises consequential protocol statements: Section 3 changes hard-training levels from 1,000 to 500 and replaces strictly unseen test levels with sampling from the full level distribution. Section 4.3 still states 1,000 levels, so the actual split and whether existing experiments were rerun remain unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's depth, aggregate dormancy, and saliency analyses, v2 adds controls examining receptive-field expansion versus projection bottlenecks, tests bottleneck changes within Impoola, localizes dormancy to individual layers, and investigates extreme-resolution saturation on Starpilot (Appendices B.1.2–B.1.4). These substantially broaden the mechanisms and limits investigated.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent seeds per environment, IQM aggregation, and 95% stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. Computational timings remain averaged over three seeds. The new Starpilot experiment uses the existing five-run practice; no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: The headline scores remain 0.674 for Impoola and 0.527 for Impala, with the same reported 28% difference. New results include improved Impala testing performance with bottleneck adaptations (Figure 15), stronger early-layer dormancy in Impala (Figure 16), and Starpilot performance peaking at resolution 224 before declining slightly at 256 (Figure 17). These are added findings, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 introduces a receptive-field recurrence and worked architectural derivation, obtaining a baseline receptive field of 141 pixels and comparing variants in Table 2. This adds a limited formal geometric analysis. The projection-size equations largely formalize v1's existing explanation of quadratic versus resolution-independent parameter growth.

C1.justification: v2 relaxes the introduction's claim that substantial gains require a resolution-independent architecture: other small architectural modifications can also enable gains, while GAP remains preferred. The abstract and conclusion also qualify the causal explanation. The central resolution-scaling contribution and reported 28% advantage remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the explanation to include bottleneck regularization, interactions between receptive-field coverage and projection size, and hypotheses linking early-layer dormancy to residual shortcuts and gradient problems. It adds qualifications about the generality of the single-game extreme-resolution findings and practical memory limits. These mechanisms are presented largely as interpretations rather than established causes.

D1.justification: v2 adds a study-code repository link, discloses learning-rate scaling by width, specifies the new architectural variants, and supplies per-layer shapes, kernels, parameter counts, and operation counts in Tables 3–4. These substantially expand reproducibility information. The benchmark repository link is retained in Appendix A.1; the added learning-rate description does not establish a changed training procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds Psychlab, implicit-attention research, DrQ-v2, and a bird's-eye-view driving reference. Related work now acknowledges earlier investigations of visual stimulus size and higher-resolution controllers, while retaining the positioning around systematic resolution scaling. The overall research framing remains similar.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, architecture explanation, RQ1 discussion, and conclusion receive localized rewrites. Appendix headings become more descriptive, B.1 gains a subsection structure, and Appendix C is added. The main section sequence and four-question narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial new displays: architectural ablation panels, six-layer dormancy plots, an extreme-resolution curve, a receptive-field table, and two detailed architecture tables. Existing plots are largely retained; v1 Figures 5–7 are reordered as v2 Figures 7, 5, and 6. The visual expansion goes beyond renumbering and pagination.

improvement.justification: The new architectural controls strengthen the evidence, and the added implementation details and less exclusive claims improve reproducibility and calibration. However, v2 introduces a 500-versus-1,000 training-level inconsistency. Its inference from parameter counts to absolute dormant-neuron counts is also unclear given that both projection layers output 256 units. These issues limit the overall gain despite the useful additional experiments.
